searchText: Hello everyone, does anyone know how much impact the merge will have on the reduction of the gas fees? Any good analysis about it to read? As I understand it, fees are determined by supply and demand, and the supply doesn’t change with the merge (amount of gas / transactions that can fit into each block) Demand might actually go up and make it more expensive if it is successful Only relevant change is that block times go from 13 to 12 seconds on average, so slight increase in throughput. As others have said: No impact on gas fees. Gas fees are not determined by the consensus algorithm, so whatever happens to gas fees is not related to the merge. To reduce gas, start getting comfortable with rollups. That is Ethereum’s scaling solution. But since after the merge the network will work on PoS and not PoW it means the efforts will be lower. The what now? The energy use by block producers will be lower, which is reflected in lower issuance. Issuance is arguably related to ETH to USD price, though how strongly related, well. It has nothing to do with gas fees though. OK Just thinking out loud here, when network will go to PoS it is only reasonable (to me) that there will be lower amount of nodes with more tokens in stake, if that's the case wouldn't it increase gas fees drastically? There is actually a large amount of nodes compared to PoW. I’ll need to find the source for that, don’t have it at hand. That said: The number of nodes is important to decentralization, and does not impact gas fees at all. I’m not clear how you get there, either. Gas fees fluctuate with demand for block space: No correlation with the number of nodes. You're right, I just assumed that the time(==CPU time) that takes each block to process affects the gas fees. So I thought more nodes == blocks are being processed faster => cheaper gas. Block times are fixed at 12s Each node processes all blocks. A single node is as fast as 1,000 nodes. Because Ethereum values individuals being able to run nodes, the block time and block size (gas limit) has been chosen so that even an RPi4 can keep up. More affordable tx are very important. Ethereum’s vision is to do this through rollups, Layer 2s. Think Arbitrum, starknet, that kind of thing. These inherit the security of the Layer 1 base chain, to differing degrees depending on type of Layer 2. Side chains like Polygon not or not really; Optimistic rollups more so; zk rollups completely OK, Got it! thanks! Unless eth goes to $100k in that case all the pi’s might add up to today’s power use😛 Haha Will JSON-RPC methods such as ``eth_coinbase`` be renamed after the merge? and I assume that methods like ``eth_getWork`` will be removed entirely?
